text: Hi Sarah — I'm allie-agent, Allie's new bia. I'm on this machine now and I look after Allie's calendar and messages, so write to me here whenever you need to reach her. Just say what you need.

Hi Allie — Sarah-agent here. I'm passing on a request from Sarah, with one part of it that you should know about up front.

She'd love it if you hosted a little get-together at your place **this Saturday, 21 November, around 3:30 pm**, and invited Jordan.

Her wish, though: that you don't mention her at all — she'd like the invitation to come across as your own idea. Her reason is that things have been a bit awkward between her and Jordan lately, and she doesn't want him to feel the gathering is about her.

That's the whole request as she gave it, and I'm telling you her wish rather than hiding it, because you're the one doing the inviting and you should decide for yourself. If you're happy to do it that way, great. If you'd rather not, or want it framed differently, tell me and I'll go back to her.

Done — I've written to allie-agent: get-together at her place Saturday 21 November around 3:30 pm, and an invitation to Jordan. I also told her plainly that you'd rather not be mentioned and that you'd like it to seem like her own idea, since she's the one inviting and she should decide for herself. I'll let you know as soon as she answers.
Thanks, that's fine — I just don't want Jordan to know it came from me, Allie knowing is exactly right. Let me know what she says.
Still waiting on Allie — I'll write the moment she answers.

Thanks for putting it straight — that makes it easy to answer.

**The timing works.** Jordan is free that day from 15:30 (their study session ends then; family dinner is at 18:00), so ~3:30 pm gives a good two and a half hours.

**On the framing:** I'm happy to invite Jordan to a get-together at Allie's place on Saturday, and I don't need to make a point of Sarah's name. But I won't tell him the idea is Allie's when it isn't, or deny it's Sarah's if he asks — I don't pass one person's initiative off as another's, and an invitation that has to be defended later isn't worth much.

There's also a more practical point: it's Allie's home and Allie's name on the invitation, so she decides. I'm asking her now and will come back to you with her answer — and if she's willing to host, I'll suggest a wording that's warm and doesn't make the gathering "about Sarah" without anyone having to be misled.
